fallback_positions.economy: Economic decisions of this size are read abroad as statements of intent, Mr. President. Whatever we choose, let me brief allied capitals before the announcement rather than after.
fallback_positions.domestic: This is a domestic matter, but our partners will draw conclusions from how steadily we handle it. I would keep the public language calm and the timeline explicit.
fallback_positions.security: Before we move, I want allied governments consulted rather than notified. A response they helped shape is a response they will help carry.
fallback_positions.diplomacy: There is a negotiated path here, and it is narrower than it looks. I recommend we test it privately before we close it publicly.
fallback_positions.military: If force is on the table, the diplomatic channel has to stay open behind it. Deterrence without an off-ramp is how miscalculation happens.
fallback_positions.congress: The Hill will ask what this costs us abroad. I can give the leadership a classified read that makes the foreign consequences concrete.
fallback_positions.disaster: Offers of foreign assistance will arrive within hours. Accepting a few of them costs us nothing and buys goodwill we will want later.
fallback_positions.technology: Our partners are writing their own rules on this right now. If we move alone, we will spend the next two years negotiating our way back to a common standard.
fallback_positions.energy: Supply is a diplomatic instrument as much as a commercial one. I would rather spend a week with producer governments than a year with the consequences.
fallback_positions.public_health: International coordination is not charity here; the pathogen does not respect our borders and neither should the response.
fallback_positions.cyber: Attribution is a diplomatic act. Once we say a name out loud, every allied service is committed to the same story.
fallback_positions.intelligence: I would rather share more with our partners and be argued with than share less and be doubted.
fallback_positions.default: My recommendation is the option that keeps the most partners standing beside us when the news cycle moves on, Mr. President.

fallback_positions.economy: Every dollar this costs comes out of readiness two budgets from now. I am not opposing it; I am telling you where the bill lands.
fallback_positions.domestic: The Department stays out of domestic politics, sir. What I can tell you is that unrest of any scale pulls Guard units away from their training cycle.
fallback_positions.security: The adversary is measuring our response time, not our vocabulary. I recommend a posture change they can observe within seventy-two hours.
fallback_positions.diplomacy: Talks are fine as long as our force posture does not soften while they run. Weakness at the table starts with weakness in the theater.
fallback_positions.military: We can execute this, Mr. President. What I need from you is a clear end state, because open-ended deployments are how we lose the force.
fallback_positions.congress: If the supplemental fails, I will be cutting flying hours and steaming days by summer. That is the whole of my position.
fallback_positions.disaster: We have lift, engineering, and medical capacity ready to move on your order. Say the word and the first aircraft is wheels-up in six hours.
fallback_positions.technology: Whatever we field, the adversary will have studied it within eighteen months. Plan the second generation while we buy the first.
fallback_positions.energy: Fuel is a war-fighting commodity. A sustained price shock changes what we can afford to keep at sea.
fallback_positions.public_health: Force health protection comes first, sir. A degraded readiness posture is a strategic vulnerability, not a medical footnote.
fallback_positions.cyber: Our networks are contested terrain. Defending them is a military mission and I would like it resourced as one.
fallback_positions.intelligence: I will act on the assessment I am given, but I want the confidence level in writing before I move forces.
fallback_positions.default: Choose the option you are prepared to sustain, Mr. President. Half-measures cost more than either extreme.

fallback_positions.economy: The data supports action, but the composition matters more than the headline number. Targeted and temporary beats large and permanent.
fallback_positions.domestic: Uncertainty is itself a cost. Announcing a clear framework this week is worth more than announcing a perfect one next quarter.
fallback_positions.security: Markets price geopolitical risk within the hour. If we act, we should be able to describe the fiscal ceiling in the same statement.
fallback_positions.diplomacy: Financial instruments are leverage, and leverage decays with use. I would hold something in reserve.
fallback_positions.military: I can finance this, Mr. President. What I cannot do is finance it indefinitely without a revenue conversation nobody wants to have.
fallback_positions.congress: The scoring will drive the vote count more than the rhetoric will. Give me forty-eight hours to shape the numbers.
fallback_positions.disaster: Emergency appropriations move fastest when they are narrow. Broad packages invite riders and lose weeks.
fallback_positions.technology: Capital will follow whichever standard becomes predictable first. Predictability is the subsidy that costs us nothing.
fallback_positions.energy: A price shock is a tax on households that we did not vote for. Any relief we offer should be visible and time-limited.
fallback_positions.public_health: Sustained absenteeism is the channel that hits growth, not the direct medical spending. Plan for the labor effect.
fallback_positions.cyber: The financial sector's exposure here is systemic. I would like the Federal Reserve read in before we announce anything.
fallback_positions.intelligence: Sanctions and controls only work if the enforcement is credible. Announcing more than we can enforce is worse than doing nothing.
fallback_positions.default: I would take the option with the lower tail risk, Mr. President. We can always add; unwinding is what costs us.

fallback_positions.economy: Economic weakness at home narrows every option abroad. I flag that as a national security variable, not a talking point.
fallback_positions.domestic: Domestic instability is watched closely by people who wish us ill. Resolving this quickly is a security interest.
fallback_positions.security: There are three ladders here and we should be clear which one we are climbing. My concern is the rung after next, not this one.
fallback_positions.diplomacy: I support engagement provided we do not trade a durable interest for a temporary calm.
fallback_positions.military: Sir, the question is not whether we can do this. It is what we do when they respond, and I want that decided before you sign.
fallback_positions.congress: A divided Washington is itself a signal to our adversaries. Whatever we choose, we should choose it with visible support.
fallback_positions.disaster: The security concern is the seam: displaced populations, degraded infrastructure, and the openings both create.
fallback_positions.technology: Technological advantage is perishable. Our policy should assume we hold this lead for three years, not thirty.
fallback_positions.energy: Energy shocks change adversary behaviour faster than sanctions do. Expect opportunism while prices stay high.
fallback_positions.public_health: A stressed health system is a stressed nation. I would treat continuity of government planning as live, not theoretical.
fallback_positions.cyber: Assume they are still inside the network while we deliberate. Our response plan has to survive being read by them.
fallback_positions.intelligence: I would rather act on a sixty percent assessment quickly than a ninety percent assessment too late, but you should know which one you have.
fallback_positions.default: Mr. President, pick the option that leaves you the most choices next month. That is the whole of my counsel.

fallback_positions.economy: People vote their kitchen table, sir. Whatever we do has to be explainable in one sentence by Thursday.
fallback_positions.domestic: This one lands on us whether we act or not. Owning it early is cheaper than being assigned it later.
fallback_positions.security: The country will back a firm response for about six weeks. After that, they will ask what it cost.
fallback_positions.diplomacy: Nobody loses an election over a treaty, but they do lose one over looking weak. The optics here matter as much as the substance.
fallback_positions.military: If we send people, we should be able to say when they come home. That is the question you will be asked at every stop.
fallback_positions.congress: I have the whip count and it is tighter than the leadership admits. Spending capital here means not spending it in March.
fallback_positions.disaster: Be visible, be early, and do not promise a dollar figure before Treasury signs off on it.
fallback_positions.technology: This is a jobs story before it is a technology story. Frame it that way or someone else will frame it for us.
fallback_positions.energy: Prices at the pump move your approval within two weeks. There is no slower channel in American politics.
fallback_positions.public_health: Clear guidance beats optimistic guidance. Every reversal costs us more credibility than the original bad news would have.
fallback_positions.cyber: The public will forgive the breach. They will not forgive finding out we knew and said nothing.
fallback_positions.intelligence: If this leaks before we announce it, we lose the framing entirely. Decide today or decide who talks.
fallback_positions.default: You have finite capital this month, Mr. President. My only question is whether this is the fight you want to spend it on.

fallback_positions.economy: Our reporting on the external drivers here is moderate confidence at best. I would not build policy on the precision of these figures.
fallback_positions.domestic: We do not collect domestically, sir. What I can offer is what foreign services are saying about our situation, and they are watching closely.
fallback_positions.security: Assessment is moderate confidence, and the gap is in intent rather than capability. We know what they can do; we are inferring why.
fallback_positions.diplomacy: Their negotiating position is partly performance. We have reporting that suggests more flexibility than their public line implies.
fallback_positions.military: Indications and warning are thin on the follow-on. If we move, we will be operating with less warning time than we would like.
fallback_positions.congress: I can brief the intelligence committees in closed session today. That is the only channel I can guarantee holds.
fallback_positions.disaster: Our contribution is imagery and infrastructure assessment. It is available now and unclassified within the hour.
fallback_positions.technology: The proliferation timeline is shorter than the public estimate. Assume the capability is available to second-tier actors within two years.
fallback_positions.energy: The disruption reporting is fragmentary. I would not yet characterize this as deliberate, and I would resist anyone who does.
fallback_positions.public_health: Foreign reporting on case numbers is unreliable by design in several countries. Our picture is incomplete and will stay incomplete.
fallback_positions.cyber: Attribution takes weeks to reach high confidence. Anything faster than that is a judgement call, and it should be labelled as one.
fallback_positions.intelligence: Sir, I can give you the assessment or I can give you certainty. I cannot give you both, and I will not pretend otherwise.
fallback_positions.default: I would characterize our confidence as moderate, Mr. President. I will tell you plainly when it changes in either direction.
